top_categories.workout_context: UCI Gravel World Championships' Minimum 80% gravel, Blackwood Valley forest and farm roads forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 88 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic UCI Gravel World Championships' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
137ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At UCI Gravel World Championships, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
12,182ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At UCI Gravel World Championships, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
12,182ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of UCI Gravel World Championships. Train it until it feels boring.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on undulating Blackwood Valley gravel and repeated. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
At mile 60 of 88, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Low-cadence force work for 12,182ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 12,182ft of climbing on undulating Blackwood Valley gravel and repeated does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for UCI Gravel World Championships’s 88 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at UCI Gravel World Championships demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride undulating blackwood valley gravel and repeated steep climbs at race-day cadence weekly. Expect: minimum 80% gravel, blackwood valley forest and farm roads, short, steep repeated climbs. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Dial in tire pressure before race week — 5 PSI wrong costs you 15+ minutes over 88 miles.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Gravel Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 88 miles of undulating blackwood valley gravel and repeated steep climbs in Nannup, Western Australia, Australia.
